reason: planning stopped before any code was written: the critic judged that the reading misread the request: The reading defines a candidate-shaped head as "governed work plus the job's candidate record", but the real early head has no candidate record in it. open_early_pr pushes the candidate commit `c`, built in crates/athena-core/src/run/candidate.rs:98-110 and run/mod.rs:480-494. That commit is the base tree plus the producer's changes only, and the candidate record is filled in afterwards with `candidate_commit = Some(c)`, so the record cannot sit inside the commit it names. So the head the first CI run sees is "a governed change with no job records". The reading's assumptions say that shape is "still judged as before", which means the reading keeps failing the exact head the request is about. Criteria 1 and 2 test a shape the early-PR flow never produces. (round 1 of 3). The plan is internally careful. It applies the rule only to the head or to a stacked landing of the same job, judges the landing in full, adds negative cases, and checks its dependents well. The prefix it matches exists at crates/athena-gate/src/history.rs:158, and check_pr_head exists at pr_check.rs:47. But it builds on a head shape that the code shows never happens. Read in the snapshot: the early pull-request head is the candidate commit from run/candidate.rs:101, which is base plus the producer's work with no records/ entries. The candidate record points at that commit by sha (candidate.rs:109). It cannot be inside it, and gh/records.rs does not push it anywhere. So `pending_candidate`, which requires the commit to add candidate.json or candidate2.json, never matches a real early head. The first CI run would still fail with exit 2, and the request's root cause would stay unfixed. The plan saw this risk but left it as an open question to the user, although the answer is readable in the code. Fixing this means redefining what makes a head "pending". It has to be identified without a record in the tree, perhaps by matching the head sha to a known candidate commit, and the plan must name where CI can see that information. That changes the accepted reading's definition and criteria 1 and 2, so the reading needs to be redone before planning. Per the role's rules, that makes the verdict reject rather than revise. Findings: blocker: The detector needs a candidate record that the real early head never contains, so the CI failure the request is about remains. (Plan step 2 (`pending_candidate`) and Decision 1; crates/athena-core/src/run/candidate.rs:98-110); major: The plan asks the user something the code already answers. (Open questions, item 2); major: The test fixtures build a fictional head, so the tests would pass while real CI still fails. (Demonstrations for criteria 1 and 2 (`candidate_head` helper, `pending_head` helper)); minor: Matching on the message text to demote a gate violation is fragile, and it works around the gate rather than fixing it there. (Plan step 4 / Decision 3 (prefix match on the history violation text))
